0x00100008.name: _start
0x00100008.why: the ELF entry point: clears the GPRs/FPRs, zeroes .bss 0x00215800-0x0039ADE0 with 128-bit stores, sets $gp = 0x0021D770, then InitMainThread/InitHeap and calls main

0x00100310.name: main
0x00100310.why: (argc, argv) from crt0; 0x90020-byte frame, runs the init sequence, returns 0

0x00103460.name: dummyNonagTest
0x00103460.why: debug harness, same shape as dummyBattleSyncTest

0x00103888.name: dummyBattleSyncTest
0x00103888.why: debug harness: builds a request+handlers+result on the stack and runs one event

0x00105160.name: dbgVPrintf
0x00105160.why: (fmt, ...) spilling a1..t3 and f12..f16 to a varargs area at sp+0x38; gated on debug bit 0x4000 like dbgPrintf. assertFail formats through it

0x001051D0.name: assertFail
0x001051D0.why: the panic call, 684 call sites -- takes (file, line, expr); every recovered assert in asserts.json comes from a call to it

0x001052A8.name: assertHalt
0x001052A8.why: 8 bytes; called on the non-reporting assert path immediately before the deliberate misaligned store that stops the machine

0x00106950.name: gameMainLoop
0x00106950.why: the frame loop; its own profiler label is 'Main Loop'. Per-tick hook at *0x00219000, quit flag at 0x00219004, frame counter 0x001D3A38, vsync counter 0x001D3A3C

0x00106DA8.name: cdGetMediaType
0x00106DA8.why: returns 1 for CD, 2 for DVD. Debug bit 0x0100 forces 1 and 0x0200 forces 2 without asking the drive; bit 0x2000 enables the real query via 0x001967A8, and with none of them set it assumes 2 (DVD), which is what this game shipped on

0x00106E28.name: cdInit
0x00106E28.why: sceCdInit(0), then the rest of disc bring-up -- unless debug bit 0x0400 is set, which returns early and skips it entirely

0x0010CC00.name: rand_below
0x0010CC00.why: (n): rand() * n, taking the high half of the 64-bit product -- a random value below n. 208 call sites

0x00111B68.name: hhcamera_get_view
0x00111B68.why: asserts objtype == HHCA_OBJTYPE, returns the view block; result is passed straight to hhcamera_set_lookat

0x00111DC0.name: hhcamera_set_lookat
0x00111DC0.why: (view, dst, fwd, up) with roll from camera+0x1D8; called on both the clamped and unclamped paths

0x00111EE8.name: hhcamera_apply_angle_limits
0x00111EE8.why: clamps the look angle to camera+0x1D0..0x1D6 and prints the CAMERA ORIG/CENTER/RANGE/MIN/MAX/LIMIT ANGLE debug rows

0x001137C8.name: hhDbgPrintRow
0x001137C8.why: (page, row, fmt, ...) -- every CAMERA %4d %4d line goes through it, rows 2..8

0x0011F858.name: AlphaSort
0x0011F858.why: the call wrapped by profilerBegin/End('AlphaSort'), run over indices 0x79..0x7F

0x001213D8.name: hhObjectEnableSet
0x001213D8.why: (obj, on): clears bit 0x10 of the flags word at obj+0x104 and sets it from (on != 0); also checks the objtype u16 at obj+0xF4 against 0x4C4D. 193 call sites. The exact semantic of bit 0x10 is inferred, the bit manipulation is not

0x00121C08.name: UpdateAll
0x00121C08.why: wrapped by the profiler label 'UpdateAll' in the main loop; unit hhobject.c agrees

0x001225F8.name: HahiGDrawAll
0x001225F8.why: opens with profilerBegin('HahiGDrawAll'); drives HahiGHierarchyAll then AlphaSort

0x00122A10.name: HahiGHierarchyAll
0x00122A10.why: the single call wrapped by profilerBegin/End('HahiGHierarchyAll')

0x00124120.name: hhObjectCmdNop
0x00124120.why: 8 bytes, `jr $ra; nop`. The default entry for unused opcodes -- it fills 12 of the 32 slots in the command table

0x001264E8.name: hhObjectCmdExec
0x001264E8.why: the hahig object command interpreter (2368 bytes). Reads a byte opcode with lbu, and for op < 0x20 indexes the 32-entry handler table at 0x001D8150; for op >= 0x20 it scans the runtime objtype registry at 0x00330BA0 instead

0x0012E410.name: ProfileBegin
0x0012E410.why: the game's own name, from an assertion in ../hahig/hhprofil.c that calls it -- supersedes the descriptive 'profilerBegin' I had used

0x0012E5E0.name: ProfileEnd
0x0012E5E0.why: the game's own name, from an assertion in ../hahig/hhprofil.c

0x00131018.name: hhtext_put_char
0x00131018.why: Called in a loop by hhtext_format_number once per output character, taking (char, style) -- the per-character emitter.

0x00131178.name: hhtext_format_number
0x00131178.why: Integer-to-string for the text system. Switches on 'd'/'x'/'X' AND their full-width Shift-JIS forms (0x8263 D, 0x8284 d, 0x8298 x), sets radix 10 or 16, extracts digits with divu/mfhi/mflo, adds 0x30, and uses +7 or +0x27 for hex letter case. Emits '-' for negatives and pads to a field width. Writes into a scratch buffer at 0x002C0290 and pushes characters through hhtext_00131018.

0x00131818.name: hhtext_parse_escape
0x00131818.why: Compares the incoming byte against 0x24 ('$') and a table of codes below 0x26 -- the handler for the script's $-escapes ($n, $m and friends). Also references the string 'text end \n'.

0x00132330.name: hhtext_draw_string
0x00132330.why: Walks a Shift-JIS string. Detects a double-byte lead with (c-0x80) < 0x20 or c < 0xE0, then combines two bytes as (c<<8)|next -- the standard SJIS test. This is the main text emitter.

0x00134B58.name: hhDrawPrintf
0x00134B58.why: varargs formatter: spills a1..t3 and f12..f15 to a stack area at +0x138, formats into a stack buffer, then draws. 207 call sites, 19 distinct format strings

0x001371F8.name: hhTaskTransTo
0x001371F8.why: (state): stores a0 as u16 at task+0x136 then tail-calls hhTaskTrans

0x00137250.name: GameTask
0x00137250.why: wrapped by the profiler label 'GameTask' in the main loop; unit hhtask.c agrees

0x0013B1D8.name: HahiGParticleDraw
0x0013B1D8.why: profiler label 'HahiGParticleDraw' at +0x78. NOTE: 0x0013B450 carries the identical label -- two variants in hhpartic.c, and which is which is not established

0x0013B450.name: HahiGParticleDraw_2
0x0013B450.why: carries the same 'HahiGParticleDraw' profiler label as 0x0013B1D8; suffixed only to keep names unique

0x0013DA80.name: Primitives
0x0013DA80.why: named by the debug-menu table at 0x00203208, whose neighbouring entries other passes already named Sprites and Tasks

0x00140048.name: SnapShotWriteBmp
0x00140048.why: reads the RTC, sprintf's 'host:%s/../temp/pic/%d%d%d%d-%d%d%d%d%d%d.bmp' from the BCD fields, opens with flags 0x602 (WRONLY|CREAT|TRUNC) and writes the image

0x00140118.name: SnapShotTask
0x00140118.why: polls the pad word at 0x00215808 each frame; while bit 0x0800 is held for 60 consecutive frames it sets the request flag at 0x002C77D8, then resets the counter

0x00140188.name: SnapShotUpdate
0x00140188.why: called every frame from gameMainLoop; when the request flag is 1 it runs the four capture steps and clears the flag

0x001401F0.name: SnapShotInit
0x001401F0.why: gated on debug bit 0x0001: clears the 0x10-byte struct at 0x002C77D8, stores the two GS framebuffer addresses 0x04000000/0x04100000, creates the task and names it 'SnapShot'

0x00140278.name: SnapShotExit
0x00140278.why: kills the task and memsets the struct

0x001408B0.name: overlayLoad
0x001408B0.why: memsets 1MB at 0x01F00000 then reads prog/<mode>.bin into it; prints "overlay '%s' loading...". Bit 0x10 of the debug flags at 0x001D3910 switches the source from the disc (0x00146FA8) to the dev host (0x001088D0)

0x00140990.name: overlayEnter
0x00140990.why: FlushCache(0) and FlushCache(2) via eeSyscall_100, then `jal 0x01F00000` with the context in a0. Its return value becomes the next mode id -- that is how modes chain

0x001433A8.name: dbgPrintf
0x001433A8.why: printf gated on bit 0x4000 of the debug flags word at 0x001D3910; 597 call sites. NOT part of adpcm.c despite the attribution

0x00146210.name: ui_place_piece
0x00146210.why: (obj, x, y) -- used nine times in a row by window_layout to place the frame corners/edges/centre, so it positions one piece of a nine-slice frame.

0x00147B78.name: ui_text_rect
0x00147B78.why: (out_rect, x, y, ncols, nrows): width = (charW+gap)*ncols, height likewise from nrows, then runs x through ui_resolve_x and y through ui_resolve_y so the 0x4000 centre sentinel works. Writes x,y,w,h to out_rect. This is THE function that decides how big any text box is.

0x00147C90.name: ui_char_advance
0x00147C90.why: charWidth + gap, i.e. how far one character advances.

0x0014B410.name: ui_obj_enable
0x0014B410.why: (handle, ...): handle-table lookup at 0x002CAAD8, then tail-calls hhObjectEnableSet(obj, 1)

0x0014B5A0.name: ui_draw_sprite
0x0014B5A0.why: takes (handle, x, y); tail-calls the two coordinate resolvers, so every sprite drawn through it accepts the 0x4000 centre sentinel.

0x0014C6B0.name: ui_obj_printf
0x0014C6B0.why: (handle, fmt, ...): looks the handle up in the table at 0x002CB2DC (handle*4, -1 means none) then formats with varargs spilled at sp+0x30. 310 call sites, 37 distinct format strings

0x0014CEB8.name: choose_text_set_pos
0x0014CEB8.why: (slot,x,y): 0x8000 leaves an axis alone, the 0x4000 bit means centre (resolved against the text's own width/height), result stored as a float at obj+0x80/+0x84 and 0x00440000 OR'd into flags at +0x104. Callers include window.c and choose.c.

0x0014D238.name: choose_text_draw_fmt
0x0014D238.why: saves eight FP registers and the integer varargs, looks a text object out of the table at 0x002CB5A0 by slot index, and calls into hhtext.c -- a printf-style text draw wrapper.

0x0014D528.name: choose_text_width
0x0014D528.why: (charW + gap) * nchars - gap, with nchars at slot+8; returns 0 for slot -1 or nchars<=0.

0x0014D5A0.name: choose_text_height
0x0014D5A0.why: same shape as choose_text_width, used for the Y axis.

0x0014D618.name: choose_text_set_colour
0x0014D618.why: packs four bytes read from a struct into an RGBA word and passes it with the slot's text object into hhtext.c.

0x0014D7F8.name: choose_menu_add_items
0x0014D7F8.why: Copies a string into the menu's buffer at +0x2448 and splits it on '\n' -- each LINE becomes one menu item. Item text pointers go to menu+0x24+i*16, count at menu+0x1024, max 0x100. Asserts 'slot->tail+strlen(src)<&slot->buff[MAXBUFF]' and 'ino<MAXITEM'.

0x0014DAB0.name: choose_menu_create
0x0014DAB0.why: (x, y, cols, rows, pitch): stores cols at menu+0x102C and rows at menu+0x1030, and defaults the 5th argument to 24 if negative. Those two numbers are what the box size is computed from later.

0x0014E900.name: choose_set_menu_pos
0x0014E900.why: (id,x,y) passes the same x,y to the menu background (+0x18), the text (+0x1c via choose_text_set_pos) and a third element (+0x20). Reached only through a function pointer, so the script layer drives it.

0x0014FBE8.name: ui_resolve_x
0x0014FBE8.why: if (x == 0x4000) x = (512 - w)/2; else x unchanged. 0x4000 is a 'centre me' sentinel and 512 is the framebuffer width.

0x0014FC10.name: ui_resolve_y
0x0014FC10.why: same shape with 448, the framebuffer height.

0x001511F0.name: choose_draw_cursor_arrows
0x001511F0.why: three ui_draw_sprite calls whose y is offset by a 40-entry triangle-wave table at 0x001DA310 (0..8..0), i.e. a bob animation. Positions come from the menu box at +0x00 with widths at +0x60/+0x64 and an align flag at +0xA4. NOT the menu text -- that was the earlier mistake.

0x00157BE8.name: gm_memory_area_load
0x00157BE8.why: (charIdx, src, len) -- bulk-loads a character's memory area from a save chunk

0x00159D20.name: global_3846C8_get
0x00159D20.why: returns *(u32*)0x003846C8, 616 call sites. Paired with global_3846C8_set; the debug harnesses save and restore it around a test. What it holds is NOT established, so the name stays descriptive

0x00159D30.name: global_3846C8_set
0x00159D30.why: stores a0 to *(u32*)0x003846C8; ignores any further argument

0x00159DA8.name: gmSaveDataInitAll
0x00159DA8.why: memsets 0x66EA0 bytes of save data then walks chunks, bounds-checking chank->header.type against 43 (sltiu 0x2b) and dispatching through datainitalfunclist at 0x001DBE00 -- the assert at gmsave.c:309 names that array

0x00159F08.name: gmSaveChunkMemory
0x00159F08.why: datainitalfunclist[2]: passes the whole payload and its length to 0x00157BE8 -- the 28000-byte per-character memory area

0x00159F28.name: gmSaveChunkCondition
0x00159F28.why: datainitalfunclist[4]: loops 5 times over s16 values. The payload is 10 bytes = 5 x u16, and the status screen shows exactly five condition stats

0x00159F88.name: gmSaveChunkSkills
0x00159F88.why: datainitalfunclist[5]: loops 4 times over s16 values, calling a (charIdx, fieldNo, value) setter. Payload is 8 bytes = 4 x u16; fields 2-4 are the guide's information / administration / close combat

0x0015A048.name: gmSaveChunkMoney
0x0015A048.why: datainitalfunclist[7]: reads the u32 payload at +8 and the character index as the u16 at +2, then calls 0x00165810

0x0015C348.name: gmModeManager
0x0015C348.why: the top-level mode loop, and the retail boot path (boot-mode table entry 0). Reads the mode id at 0x00317BE8, looks the overlay path up in the table at 0x001DC338, runs it, and reports memory held per mode. Initialises the id to 1 (title)

0x00165810.name: gm_money_set
0x00165810.why: (charIdx, amount) -- the only call in gmSaveChunkMoney

0x00165A88.name: gm_skill_set
0x00165A88.why: (charIdx, fieldNo, value) -- called four times by gmSaveChunkSkills

0x0016BA68.name: window_layout
0x0016BA68.why: Lays out the dialogue box. Gets the text rect, then grows it by 10px on the left/top and 18px in width/height (so 8px on the right/bottom) -- that is the border padding. Places the nine frame pieces (obj+0x1c..+0x40) around it, positions the text with choose_text_set_pos at the ORIGINAL x,y, and finally draws the page-break arrow at (x+8, y+6).

0x0016DAA8.name: evsStep
0x0016DAA8.why: return ctx->buffer + ctx->body[ctx->pc] -- proves ctx->0x18 is a u32 offset table indexed by the PC

0x0016DBA8.name: evsIsOp1
0x0016DBA8.why: *(u16*)evsStep() == 1 -- dialogue; half of all script steps in the game

0x0016DD88.name: evsStepField4
0x0016DD88.why: returns *(u32*)(evsStep() + 4) -- the word after the opcode

0x0016DEB0.name: evsCallHook20
0x0016DEB0.why: jalr on ctx->request->0x0C->0x20 -- the event object carries its own callbacks

0x0016FDE8.name: gmEventSequenceExec
0x0016FDE8.why: prints gmEventSequenceExecresult = %d and calls the sequencer body

0x0016FE28.name: evseqRun
0x0016FE28.why: (request, result, x) -- the event entry point; both debug harnesses call it after building a 0x74-byte request

0x00170390.name: evseqCreate
0x00170390.why: loads event/<cat><id>.har, validates the .EVS magic, fills the context at 0x001DE41C

0x00170680.name: evseqDestroy
0x00170680.why: frees the .evs buffer and archive; the failure path of evseqCreate jumps here

0x00172108.name: evsWalkOp1
0x00172108.why: walks op-1 steps and calls a caller-supplied callback through $fp (a3)

0x001725C8.name: evsRunSteps
0x001725C8.why: the interpreter loop: advances ctx->pc and dispatches ops 1/140/141/145/146 by predicate chain

0x00172D78.name: evseqBranchIfEq
0x00172D78.why: if (ctx->request->0x18 == c) pc += then_delta; else pc += else_delta

0x00173F58.name: evseqBranchIfEq2
0x00173F58.why: same, with a compound test on request +0x18 and +0x10

0x00179D78.name: SidToSeSelect
0x00179D78.why: 93-case switch on a scene id selecting one of the 152-byte SidToSe* mappers and its entry count

0x00180330.name: gm_condition_set
0x00180330.why: (charIdx, fieldNo, value) -- called five times by gmSaveChunkCondition

0x001967A8.name: sceCdGetDiskType
0x001967A8.why: its result is compared against 0x12 and 0x14, the PS2 CD and DVD disc-type constants

0x001969A8.name: readRtc
0x001969A8.why: fills an 8-byte BCD time structure; SnapShotWriteBmp splits its nibbles into the filename digits

0x00198988.name: vec3_normalize
0x00198988.why: called on the camera delta vector immediately before asinf/atan2f

0x0019A020.name: eeSyscall_60_InitMainThread
0x0019A020.why: called from _start as (gp, stack, size, args) and its return becomes $sp -- that identifies syscall 60 by use, not by guess

0x001A3110.name: exit
0x001A3110.why: crt0 tail-calls it with main's return value, and again with 0

0x001B5360.name: asinf
0x001B5360.why: 6-instruction leaf; fed the normalised -dy of the look vector, result printed as the X of CAMERA ORIG ANGLE

0x001B5378.name: atan2f
0x001B5378.why: 6-instruction leaf; fed (dx, dz), result printed as the Y of CAMERA ORIG ANGLE

0x001BD148.name: memset
0x001BD148.why: replicates a1's low byte across a 128-bit register and stores in bulk; called as (ptr, 0, size) throughout

0x001BDCE0.name: rand
0x001BDCE0.why: LCG whose multiplier is 0x5851F42D4C957F2D, the standard constant -- identified by that alone

0x001BE248.name: sprintf
0x001BE248.why: a0 is the destination, a2..t0 are spilled to a varargs area at sp+0x90; receives 58 distinct format strings

0x001BEBB0.name: strncmp
0x001BEBB0.why: used by TaskMan to compare task names with n = 15

0x001D8150.name: hhObjectCmdTable
0x001D8150.why: 32 entries, opcode 0x00-0x1F -> handler; 21 distinct, the other 12 slots are hhObjectCmdNop

0x001DA310.name: cursor_bob_table
0x001DA310.why: 40 signed bytes, 0,0,0,0,1,1,2,2,...,8,8,8,8,...,0 -- a triangle wave, amplitude 8px, indexed by a frame counter at menu+0xA0 mod 40.

0x001DBE00.name: datainitalfunclist
0x001DBE00.why: 43-entry save-chunk initialiser table, indexed by chank->header.type; the name is the game's own, from the assert at gmsave.c:309, and the bound is proven by the sltiu 0x2b that guards it

0x001DC338.name: g_overlayPathTable
0x001DC338.why: mode id -> 'prog/<name>.bin', indexed 1..5; entry 0 is null

0x00317BE8.name: g_currentModeId
0x00317BE8.why: 1=TITLE 2=FREE 3=BATTLE 4=ENDING 5=MINIGAME; set to 1 by gmModeManager at startup

0x00330BA0.name: hhObjectTypeHandlers
0x00330BA0.why: runtime-registered dispatch keyed by the object type tag: 12-byte entries with the u16 tag at +0 and a function pointer at +8, count in the word at 0x00215830. In .bss, so it is empty in the image and invisible to static scans

_comment: Names established by reading the disassembly, with the evidence for each. Applied by tools/apply_manual.py. Kept separate from names RECOVERED from strings in the binary, which are literal developer names; these are descriptive and chosen here.

0x01F00000.name: overlayMain
0x01F00000.why: the overlay's entry point: overlayEnter jals 0x01F00000 directly, and the return value is the next mode id

0x01F5B278.name: imstrlist
0x01F5B278.why: 956-entry IM name table; the game's own identifier, from the assert at btim319.c:652, with the 955 bound proven by the sltiu that guards it

0x01F619E0.name: atkdata
0x01F619E0.why: 51 x 36-byte attack records (assert btattack.c:174). CONFIRMED against the official guide p.049: +0x04 is attack power (8/8 exact) and +0x10 is charge time in frames (/60 = the guide's printed seconds, exact on every plotted tick). +0x08 is a 16.16 reciprocal, round(65536/n) for n in {3,4,12,36,45,60,120} -- the FIRING INTERVAL, not charge. See notes/atkdata.md

0x01F62390.name: equipdata
0x01F62390.why: 13 x 40-byte battle equipment records; named by the assert at btequip.c:59, bound confirmed by the code's check and by the 13 name pointers at a 40-byte stride. +0x18 durability, +0x10/+0x14 movement multipliers and +0x0C melee/ranged are pinned by the in-game descriptions; +0x04/+0x08/+0x1C/+0x20 are not. See notes/equipdata.md

0x01F63E80.name: viewparam
0x01F63E80.why: 4-entry camera view parameter table named by the assert at btmap.c:416 (vmode>=0 && vmode<Arraysize(viewparam)); holds floats
